title: 5 takeaways from Day 13 of Patriots training camp
author: Khari A. Thompson
bullets: Carlton Davis and Will Campbell returned to Patriots practice, while Christian Barmore missed his second consecutive session.
Romeo Doubs made a highlight touchdown catch, while Kyle Williams impressed with speed and received a deep pass.
Marcus Jones highlighted the Patriots' transition from 'hunter to hunted' with the team emphasizing continuous improvement.

title: Lifeguard dragged underwater by white shark at Maine beach
author: Madison Lucchesi
bullets: A Scarborough Beach lifeguard was pulled underwater by a white shark while using a rescue torpedo on Saturday.
The lifeguard freed himself and safely swam to shore; the beach was closed for an hour following the incident.
Residents were reminded of increased shark sightings and advised to use caution when entering the water.

title: Payton Pritchard talks Jaylen Brown trade, contract extension with Celtics
author: Conor Ryan
bullets: Payton Pritchard discusses losing Jaylen Brown to the 76ers and his increased role with the Celtics.
Pritchard won the Sixth Man of the Year Award in 2024-25 and had a career-high 17 points per game in 2025-26.
Pritchard has two years left on a four-year, $30 million contract and could renegotiate an extension next year.

title: A Fall River 911 call said a man had killed his parents and had children hostage. It turned out to be a hoax.
author: Madison Lucchesi
bullets: A hoax 911 call claimed a man killed his parents and held children hostage in Fall River.
The Fall River Police established a perimeter and dispatched their Emergency Services Unit in response.
Police are investigating to identify the caller, who faces charges for making a false report.

title: Police to increase patrols downtown amid safety concerns, neighborhood group says
author: Ross Cristantiello
bullets: Boston police will increase patrols downtown due to recent violent incidents, including a murder near Boylston and Tremont streets.
The Downtown Boston Neighborhood Association identified key areas to enhance police visibility, such as Brewer Fountain Plaza and Winter Street.
Efforts to address public safety challenges include increasing police presence and enforcing city ordinances against encampments and unpermitted sales.

title: All four ‘Lord of the Rings’ movie Hobbits explored Boston together this weekend
author: Lauren Daley
bullets: Sean Astin, Elijah Wood, Dominic Monaghan, and Billy Boyd reunited in Boston for the Fan Expo and a 25th anniversary celebration.
The actors dined at La Royal Cambridge and Neptune Oyster, and visited The Green Dragon, Boston's historic Irish pub.
Monaghan noted their reunion in Boston included selfies with American history statues and denied claims of them looking unrecognizable.

title: Jaylen Brown to host free Boston block party at Boston Common on Aug. 30
author: Annie Jonas
bullets: Jaylen Brown will host '741 Frequency Fest' at Boston Common on August 30 from 2 p.m. to 7 p.m.
The event celebrates Brown's tenure with the Celtics before his trade to the Philadelphia 76ers.
The block party features music, games, giveaways, and a special concert, free for the public.

title: Patriots trade OL Caedan Wallace to Dolphins
author: Hayden Bird
bullets: Patriots traded offensive lineman Caedan Wallace and a 2029 seventh-round pick to Dolphins for a 2028 sixth-round pick.
Wallace, 26, played 10 games over the 2024 and 2025 seasons with diminished playing time last year.
The trade leaves quarterback Drake Maye and cornerback Marcellas Dial Jr. as last 2024 Patriots draft picks on the roster.

title: Comedian Matt Rife throws down with a paranormal investigator over ‘haunted’ event in Salem
author: Elizabeth Mehler
bullets: Comedian Matt Rife faced backlash after telling a paranormal investigator to commit suicide in a now-deleted comment.
Rife and Elton Castee are organizing a 'Haunted Warren Museum' event in Salem featuring items like the Annabelle doll.
Investigator Chris Mac criticized Rife's comments, calling them 'nonsense garbage', while Mac's supporters defended him online.

title: Hunter Henry agrees to a two-year extension with the Patriots
author: Hayden Bird
bullets: Hunter Henry, 31, agrees to a two-year contract extension with the New England Patriots worth up to $20 million.
The extension includes $14.5 million guaranteed and a $4.2 million signing bonus, according to reports from ESPN.
Since joining the Patriots in 2021, Henry has made 259 catches and 26 touchdowns, becoming a key offensive player.
